description: The test seeds a 12-turn conversation at /c/{{SLUG}} whose first two user messages have data-message-id {{FIRST}} and {{SECOND}}; the URL fragments that link to them are {{FIRST_FRAGMENT}} and {{SECOND_FRAGMENT}}. window.fragmentScrolls lists the data-message-id of every element scrolled into view so far, in order; check it with an eval of JSON.stringify(window.fragmentScrolls). Call "append" sends another message and waits for its reply; after it, {{APPENDED}} is the reply's data-message-id. To "set the fragment to X", eval a promise that sets location.hash to X and resolves on the next hashchange event. "At the bottom" means the messages container (".messages-container") has scrollHeight - clientHeight - scrollTop below 5 and the scroll-to-bottom button (".scroll-to-bottom-button") is hidden. To "delay" a message, rename its data-message-id attribute to data-delayed-message-id, as if its element had not mounted yet; to "mount" it, set data-message-id back from data-delayed-message-id (leaving the other attribute). Perform the steps in order. A fresh conversation keeps bottom restoration through startup clamps. Navigate to /c/{{SLUG}} and wait for the table of contents button (".toc-button") to be visible. It should be at the bottom. Then, in one async eval: in the messages container, insert a 600px-tall div into ".messages-list" just before ".messages-bottom-sentinel"; wait two animation frames; set the container's scrollTop to its scrollHeight; wait two more animation frames; remove the div; read the container's scrollTop; dispatch a "scroll" event on the container and a "beforeunload" event on window; and return localStorage.getItem("shelley_scroll_{{ID}}"). It must return "bottom". It should still be at the bottom afterwards.
